188: One who kills his children: One who causes the death of the fetus, with which his wife becomes pregnant, in her womb. He destroys the Holy One, blessed be He's, structure and His craft. There is one who kills people, but this one kills his children!

He does three evils that the entire world cannot tolerate, and it is for this that the world melts away slowly, and it is unknown; the Holy One, blessed be He, removes Himself from the world; and war, famine, and death come to the world. And these are them: He kills his children, he destroys the King's structure, and He pushes away the divine presence, which [then] goes and wanders in the world without finding rest. And because of them (it), the spirit of holiness cries (another textual version: He creates winds of holiness), and the world is punished with all these verdicts. Woe to that man, woe is to him; it would have been better if he had not been created in the world!

Meritorious is the Jewish people. For even though they were in the Egyptian exile, they guarded themselves from all three of these: From [having conjugal relations with] a menstruant woman, from the daughter of a foreign god, and from killing offspring, but they [instead] made public efforts to be fruitful and multiply. As even though Pharaoh decreed a decree — Every boy that is born, you shall throw into the Nile (Exodus 1:22) — none was found among them who killed a fetus in a woman's womb. All the more so afterward. And the Jewish people went out of exile in the merit of this.
